title: Enforce task read API view authorization and safe remote defaults
description:
Problem: task read endpoints are currently accessible without explicit view-policy authorization and were confirmed reachable without auth headers in runtime probes. Under permissive profile combinations (for example remote-enabled local development), this can expose task metadata unexpectedly.

Desired outcome: task read APIs require explicit viewer authorization semantics and remote-enabled startup refuses insecure combinations unless explicitly acknowledged by operator policy.

Scope:
- In scope: apply `CanViewMemorySmith` (or stricter) policy to task read endpoints, align middleware/startup guardrails for `AllowRemoteApi` + auth/key combinations, and add regression tests for unauthenticated access behavior by profile.
- Out of scope: full auth subsystem redesign.

Acceptance criteria:
- `GET /api/tasks` and `GET /api/tasks/{id}` enforce configured viewer authorization policy.
- Remote-enabled profile with missing required auth controls fails fast or emits explicit operator-blocking diagnostics.
- Test matrix covers anonymous, viewer, editor, and admin behavior across local and remote profiles.

Validation:
- Add integration tests verifying unauthorized callers receive expected 401/403 where appropriate.
- Verify authorized viewer/editor/admin callers retain expected read behavior.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from continued audit finding C-008 after runtime confirmation of unauthenticated task-read API access.
